why: The rewrite does not use De Morgan's law, still keeps the !( ), and chains the comparisons as in maths (5 < n < 10), which does not compile in Java, so every rule the answer applies conflicts with Java.

concepts.quote: You could write b as !(5 < n < 10).
concepts.why: It makes no correct De Morgan claim: the negation is not moved inside, the comparisons are not flipped to n <= 5 || n >= 10, and && is not swapped for ||.
It writes a range the maths way (ChainedComparison misconception); in Java 5 < n gives a boolean, so boolean < 10 does not compile.
